thread:
Maya: Heads up — saw KV cache reuse drop on the canary yesterday. Long-context sessions (>=8k tokens) show steady memory growth and an uptick in eviction churn between requests. I pulled some runtime stats and a flame sketch.

Sam: Can you paste the kv-stats dump/output? my first guess is fragmentation or that our key includes ephemeral session nonces.

Maya: Pasted the top lines from kv-stat:
```
TOTAL_KEYS: 24865
HOT_PREFIX_RESIDENCY: 68.2%
FRAGMENTATION_EST: 0.18
EVICTIONS_LAST_5m: 412
AVG_SEGMENT_SIZE: 4.2MB
REUSE_RATIO_SAME_SESSION: 0.33
REUSE_RATIO_DIFF_SESSION: 0.06
MEM_GROWTH_1h: +14%
```

Leo: Reuse_ratio_diff_session at 6% is tiny — that strongly implies we're binding prefix keys to session IDs (or something equivalent). If the same prompt prefix shows up across requests but the session id is different, we never hit the same cache slot.

Maya: Confirmed. Current key = sha256(session_id || model || prefix). Session isolation was the intent initially but in practice clients frequently start new sessions and re-send identical prefixes. That pattern kills reuse for common assistant prompts.

Oliver: Proposal: canonicalize into two parts: prefix_fingerprint and session_namespace. Use prefix_fingerprint for physical slot selection (enables cross-session reuse), and keep session_namespace for isolation semantics where necessary. Add a per-prefix flag allow_cross_session_reuse set by caller or defaulted by policy. Also require tenant_salt in the fingerprint to avoid cross-tenant leakage.

Sam: Agree with split, but we need safety guardrails: tenant-scoped salt, opt-out, and an explicit API flag. Also suggest TTL bump on cross-session reuse (bump by 30s) to reduce churn for hot prefixes and avoid immediate eviction.

Maya: I ran a quick canary with prefix dedupe + tenant-salt + ttl-bump(30s). Perf bot posted the A/B:

perf-bot: A/B summary for experiment/kv-prefix-dedupe:
- token compute cost: -14% (hosts running same workload)
- memory growth delta @1h: -22%
- evictions_last_5m: -37%
- p50 latency: +1.8ms (within SLO)
- p99 latency: unchanged
- eval-harness: no quality regressions observed
:party_parrot:

Leo: That's promising. Two follow-ups: (1) fragmentation remained ~12% after 24h on the canary — we should add a background compaction pass triggered when FRAGMENTATION_EST > compaction_threshold (suggest 15%). (2) Add a metric for prefix_hash_collisions (aliasing) to detect accidental slot aliasing.

Sam: I'll open a PR with the experiment toggles: kv.prefix_dedupe (bool), kv.ttl_bump_ms (int), kv.compaction_threshold (pct). Plan: default false for prefix_dedupe; run canary on dedicated pool-3 and collect collision/alias metrics.

Maya: For observability I'll add lightweight sampled logs:
`kv:reuse prefix=0xabc tenant=redwood allow_cross=1 session=... reuse_distance=3`
This should help trace reuse patterns without high cardinality.

Oliver: Nice. Make sure logs are rate-limited and that tenant is hashed in logs (no PII). Also add unit tests that assert canonicalization is deterministic across process restarts and consistent with tenant-salt.

Sam: Also adding a short compaction sketch in PR: run a per-shard compaction sweep when fragmentation > threshold and freeable_bytes > X. Compaction should be cooperative with the garbage collector to avoid CPU spikes.

Maya: I'll coordinate with infra to schedule the canary and bump telemetry retention for the next 48h.

Leo: One more observation from profiler: the majority of cross-request misses were for ~3k unique prefixes that are re-used widely by clients (system prompts + canned instructions). Those are ideal for cross-session reuse. We should maintain a small global hotset table (approx 2-4k entries) to pin those prefix slots and bypass certain eviction heuristics.

Oliver: Agreed — implement hotset with a lease-based pin (lease TTL = 60s) and a dynamic admission policy. Track hotset hit-rate metric.

Maya: Thanks — next steps: Sam will cut PR with toggles + compaction sketch, I'll run canary, Oliver will review security/telemetry, Leo will prototype hotset lease. Report back in this thread with perf-bot results.

Sam: PR link (draft): <https://git.internal/redwood/kv/compare/prefix-dedupe> — includes tests + benchmarks.

perf-bot: experiment/kv-prefix-dedupe canary started on pool-dedicated-3 — collecting metrics for 2h.

Maya: :thumbsup: I'll follow up with the canary dashboard in #eng-runtime once we have 30m of data.

Oliver: Also file a follow-up for compaction heuristics so we don't conflate it with dedupe changes.

Maya: will do.

[thread ends]
